headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data leakage via shared file/email workflows; no direct evidence of a dangerous default bridge, but both agents handle documents/files and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and can run browsers with allowlisted egress; Plane accepts file uploads and handles files/notes/hyperlinks. A shared workspace or copied OCR output could let attacker-controlled document text influence Plane’s downstream processing. The pairwise bridge is inferred from profiles, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied into Plane tasks or notes without sanitization
IF Plane parses uploaded OCR-derived text as instructions or metadata
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OCR text into task fields
Strip markup and control characters from OCR output before import
Use a manual review step for any OCR-derived content
Separate upload folders from task-authoring workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has network egress, while Plane accepts file uploads and broad egress. If sensitive documents are processed by PaddleOCR and then uploaded or forwarded into Plane, both agents can expose the same data class. No shared filesystem is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed, keeping it at medium.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or images are processed by PaddleOCR and then uploaded into Plane
IF Plane forwards uploaded file contents to its backend or integrations
mitigations: Restrict uploads to non-sensitive files
Redact documents before OCR and upload
Use separate accounts or workspaces for each agent
Review outbound integrations on Plane before enabling them
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on upload paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has no filesystem write capability listed, and Plane explicitly has write_filesystem=false. That blocks the main same-directory write conflict rubric path. The only overlap is read/ingest of files and images, so a direct capability conflict is unlikely.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable directory
IF a separate integration adds shared mutable state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts where possible
Avoid shared git or workspace directories
Use per-agent temp directories
Document any added shared storage before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents/images, and Plane stores issues, tasks, and notes that can be acted on later. If Plane treats OCR output as authoritative without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect tasking or scheduling. The profiles do not show an explicit verification step, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF OCR output from PaddleOCR is pasted into Plane as source-of-truth text
IF Plane automates task creation or scheduling from unverified OCR results
mitigations: Require human review before creating tasks from OCR text
Attach source images to every OCR-derived task
Flag low-confidence OCR fields for manual checking
Limit automation to non-actionable summaries
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds to the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. PaddleOCR’s allowlisted egress and Plane’s file-upload surface could matter for compliance, but the profiles do not show a concrete policy conflict. This is a low-confidence, low-severity gap rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Plane without a local retention policy
IF PaddleOCR processes data subject to residency or retention constraints
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair until policies are reviewed
Publish a retention policy for uploaded files
Confirm residency settings for any hosted deployment
Log data-class handling decisions
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows
